problem_summary.summary: Reverse the order of non-space words and normalize separators to exactly one space, with no leading or trailing spaces.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a string containing letters, digits, and spaces, with at least one word. Return the normalized reversed-word string.
constraints: s contains English letters, digits, and spaces
At least one word is present

brute_force.explanation: Split on one or more spaces, walk the resulting words backward, and join them with a single space. This is concise but allocates a token array and intermediate strings.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Splitting removes the spacing separators, and appending tokens in reverse index order reverses the word sequence. Adding separators only between tokens normalizes whitespace.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — splitting and rebuilding scan a total of O(n) characters.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the word array and returned string.

optimized.explanation: Scan the original string from right to left. Skip spaces, identify each contiguous word, and append its characters to a result builder with one separator between words. This avoids a separate array of tokens.
optimized.correctness_idea: The backward scan encounters words in reverse order. It skips all separator runs and copies only non-space spans, placing one separator between successive spans, which produces exactly the required output.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each input character is examined at most a constant number of times.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the returned string; O(1) extra working space apart from its builder.

steps.action: Move left to the final character of blue at index 11.
Append blue; continue scanning from index 7.

steps.condition: The remaining leading spaces at indices 1 and 0 are skipped and the index becomes negative.

edge_cases.handling: The scan skips them without appending separators.
Each run is skipped and replaced by one output space.
The word is appended once with no extra separator.
